what: Practical Example: Optimizing the Matching Process
title: Optimizing the Matching Process with a Random Search Algorithm
text: Matching observations based generalized propensity scores involves tuning multiple hyperparameters. Running separate workflows different parameter combinations can tedious, effects parameters always predictable. streamline process, vecmatch provides automated optimization workflow using random search algorithm. function optimize_gps() implemented multithreading leverage computational resources efficiently. Step 1: Define Formula, Data, Optimization Space example, use built-cancer dataset focus two predictors: categorical variable sex continuous variable age. first specify model formula. Note data formula fixed inputs; want compare different formulas, must run workflow separately . Next, define search space hyperparameters. helper function make_opt_args() validates inputs computes Cartesian product specified values, reporting total number parameter combinations. print() method make_opt_args() provides clear summary search space, including hyperparameter’s values total number combinations.
code: opt_args <- make_opt_args(   data            = cancer,   formula         = formula_cancer,   reference       = c("control", "adenoma", "crc_benign", "crc_malignant"),   gps_method      = c("m1", "m7", "m8"),   matching_method = c("fullopt", "nnm"),   caliper         = seq(0.01, 5, 0.01),   cluster         = 1:3,   ratio           = 1:3,   min_controls    = 1:3,   max_controls    = 1:3 )  opt_args #> Optimization Argument Set (class: opt_args) #> ----------------------------------------  #> gps_method      : m1, m7, m8 #> reference       : control, adenoma, crc_benign, crc_malignant #> matching_method : fullopt, nnm #> caliper         : [500 values] #> order           : desc, asc, original, random #> cluster         : 1, 2, 3 #> replace         : TRUE, FALSE #> ties            : TRUE, FALSE #> ratio           : 1, 2, 3 #> min_controls    : 1, 2, 3 #> max_controls    : 1, 2, 3 #> ----------------------------------------  #> Total combinations: 1512000

title: Optimizing the Matching Process with a Random Search Algorithm
text: search space defined, can launch optimization. optimize_gps() function performs random search across parameter grid returns summary table containing key quality metrics tested combination. control number iterations via n_iter argument. function uses multithreading (via future package) parallelize work. guideline, aim least 1000–1500 iterations per core reliable search coverage. Monitor system’s memory usage, since parallel backend can consume substantial amounts RAM. function uses already registered backends. default, optimize_gps() preserves global random seed. reproducibility, set seed calling optimizer. ran optimization single core n_iter = 1500; test machine required 409.26 seconds. Given size parameter grid, increasing n_iter improve search’s coverage, limited iterations keep vignette’s build time reasonable. print opt_results, summarizes entire search grouping parameter sets bins defined maximum standardized mean difference (SMD), within bin highlights combination achieves highest proportion matched observations.

what: Filter the Data Based on Common Support Region — csregion
title: Filter the Data Based on Common Support Region — csregion
text: csregion() function estimates boundaries rectangular common support region, defined Lopez Gutman (2017), filters matrix generalized propensity scores based boundaries. function returns matrix observations whose generalized propensity scores lie within treatment group-specific boundaries.

title: Filter the Data Based on Common Support Region — csregion
code: csregion(gps_matrix, borders = "include", refit = TRUE)

title: Filter the Data Based on Common Support Region — csregion
text: gps_matrix object classes gps data.frame (e.g., created estimate_gps() function). first column corresponds treatment grouping variable, columns represent treatment assignment probabilities calculated separately hypotetical treatment group. number columns therefore equal number unique levels treatment variable plus one (treatment variable ). number rows correspond number subjects generalized propensity scores estimated. borders character string specifying handle observations edges Common Support Region (CSR). Acceptable values "include" "exclude". "include" selected (default), observations Generalized Propensity Scores (GPS) exactly equal CSR boundaries retained analysis. corresponds non-strict inequality: lower_bound <= GPS <= upper_bound. "exclude" selected, observations lying exactly CSR boundaries removed. corresponds strict inequality: lower_bound <   GPS < upper_bound. Using "exclude" typically result slightly smaller matched sample size compared "include", may preferred conservative matching. refit Logical. TRUE (default), model used estimate GPS refitted excluding samples outside common support region, using formula method original estimate_gps() call. FALSE, model refitted, still samples within CSR retained. Refitting recommended, suggested Lopez Gutman (2017).

title: Filter the Data Based on Common Support Region — csregion
text: numeric matrix similar one returned estimate_gps(), number rows reduced exclude observations fit within common support region (CSR) boundaries. returned object also possesses additional attributes summarize calculation process CSR boundaries: filter_matrix - logical matrix dimensions gps-part gps_matrix, indicating treatment assignment probabilities fall within CSR boundaries, filter_vector - vector indicating whether observation kept (TRUE) removed (FALSE), essentially row-wise sum filter_matrix, csr_summary - summary CSR calculation process, including details boundaries number observations filtered. csr_data - original dataset used estimation generalized propensity scores (original_data attribute gps object) filtered filter_vector

title: Calculate Treatment Allocation Probabilities — estimate_gps
text: data frame class gps number columns equal number unique treatment variable levels plus one (treatment variable ) number rows equal number subjects initial dataset. original dataset used estimation can accessed original_data attribute.

title: Calculate Treatment Allocation Probabilities — estimate_gps
text: main goal estimate_gps() function calculate generalized propensity scores aka. treatment allocation probabilities. first step workflow vector matching algorithm essential analysis. returned matrix class gps can passed csregion() function calculate rectangular common support region boundaries drop samples eligible analysis. list available methods operated estimate_gps() provided short description function used calculations: multinom - multinomial logistic regression model nnet::multinom() vglm - vector generalized linear model multinomial data VGAM::vglm(), brglm2 - bias reduction model multinomial responses using Poisson trick brglm2::brmultinom(), mblogit - baseline-category logit models mclogit::mblogit(). polr - ordered logistic probit regression ordered factor variables MASS::polr(). method argument underlying MASS::polr() package function can controlled link argument. Available options: link = c("logistic", "probit", "loglog", "cloglog",   "cauchit")

title: Calculate Treatment Allocation Probabilities — estimate_gps
code: ## Example 1: multinomial bias-reduced model (brglm2) on `airquality` if (requireNamespace("brglm2", quietly = TRUE)) {   library(brglm2)    # Initial imbalance of means   tapply(airquality$Wind, airquality$Month, mean, na.rm = TRUE)    # Formula definition   formula_air <- Month ~ Wind    # Estimating the generalized propensity scores using brglm2   gp_scores <- estimate_gps(     formula_air,     data = airquality,     method = "brglm2",     reference = "5",     verbose_output = TRUE,     control = brglm2::brglmControl(type = "MPL_Jeffreys")   )    # Filtering the observations outside the csr region   gps_csr <- csregion(gp_scores)   filter_which <- attr(gps_csr, "filter_vector")   filtered_air <- airquality[filter_which, ]    # Imbalance after csr   tapply(filtered_air$Wind, filtered_air$Month, mean, na.rm = TRUE)    # Visual inspection using raincloud   raincloud(     filtered_air,     y = Wind,     group = Month,     significance = "t_test"   ) } #> Warning: Some groups have fewer than 20 observations, which may impact the performance of the matching process. Consider using `replace = TRUE`in `match_gps()` to address this. #> Registered S3 methods overwritten by 'ggpp': #>   method                  from    #>   heightDetails.titleGrob ggplot2 #>   widthDetails.titleGrob  ggplot2   ## Example 2: ordered treatment, subset, by, and non-default link if (requireNamespace("MASS", quietly = TRUE)) {   library(MASS)    # Prepare a clean subset of `airquality`   aq <- subset(     airquality,     !is.na(Month) & !is.na(Wind) & !is.na(Temp)   )    # Grouping variable used in the `by` argument   aq$Temp_group <- ifelse(     aq$Temp > stats::median(aq$Temp, na.rm = TRUE),     "high",     "low"   )    # Explicit order for the (ordinal) treatment variable   ord_month <- sort(unique(aq$Month))    gps_ord <- estimate_gps(     Month ~ Wind + Temp,     data = aq,     method = "polr",     link = "probit",     subset = NULL,     by = "Temp_group",     ordinal_treat = ord_month,     reference = "5"   ) } #> Warning: There is no need to specify `reference` if `ordinal_treat` was provided. Lopez Gutman (2017) explicitly specify matching algorithm used, assumed applied commonly used k-nearest neighbors matching algorithm, implemented method = "nnm". However, algorithm can sometimes challenging use, especially treatment control groups unequal sizes. replace = FALSE, number matches strictly limited smaller group, even replace = TRUE, results may always satisfactory. address limitations, implemented additional matching algorithm maximize number matched observations within dataset. available matching methods : "nnm" – classic k-nearest neighbors matching, implemented using Matching::Matchby(). tunable parameters match_gps() caliper, ratio, replace, order, ties. Additional arguments can passed Matching::Matchby() via ... argument. "fullopt" – optimal full matching algorithm, implemented optmatch::fullmatch(). method calculates discrepancy matrix identify possible matches, often optimizing percentage matched observations. available tuning parameters caliper, min_controls, max_controls. "pairmatch" – optimal 1:1 1:k matching algorithm, implemented using optmatch::pairmatch(), actually wrapper around optmatch::fullmatch(). Like "fullopt", method calculates discrepancy matrix finds matches minimize sum. available tuning parameters caliper ratio. method accepts tuning parameters listed . title: Match the Data Based on Generalized Propensity Scores — match_gps
code: # Step 1.) Estimation of the generalized propensity scores gp_scores <- estimate_gps(   formula(status ~ age * sex),   data = cancer,   method = "multinom",   reference = "control",   verbose_output = TRUE ) #> # weights:  20 (12 variable) #> initial  value 1696.824298  #> iter  10 value 1675.784597 #> final  value 1675.690057  #> converged  # Step 2.) Defining the common support region gps_csr <- csregion(gp_scores) #> # weights:  20 (12 variable) #> initial  value 1669.098411  #> iter  10 value 1648.708826 #> final  value 1646.780796  #> converged  # Example 1: optimal full matching ("fullopt") with explicit tuning params matched_cancer_full <- match_gps(   gps_csr,   caliper = 0.25,   reference = "control",   method = "fullopt",   kmeans_cluster = 2,   kmeans_args = list(     iter.max = 200,     algorithm = "Forgy"   ),   min_controls = 0,   max_controls = Inf,   order = "desc",   verbose_output = TRUE )  # Example 2: nearest neighbour matching ("nnm") demonstrating ratio / # replace / order / ties matched_cancer_nnm <- match_gps(   gps_csr,   caliper = 0.25,   reference = "control",   method = "nnm",   ratio = 2,   replace = TRUE,   order = "asc",   ties = TRUE,   verbose_output = FALSE )

Frequencies contingency table represented tiles (rectangles), tile's size proportional frequency corresponding group within entire dataset. x-axis scale remains fixed across mosaic plots, enabling straightforward comparisons imbalance across treatment groups.

text: data non-empty data.frame containing least one numeric column, specified y argument. argument must provided default value. y single string unquoted symbol representing name numeric column data. vector matching workflow, typically numeric covariate requires balancing. group single string unquoted symbol representing name factor character column data. raincloud() plots, groups specified group argument distinguished separate fill color aesthetics. clarity, recommended plot fewer 10 groups, though formal limit. facet single string unquoted symbol representing name variable data facet . argument used call ggplot2::facet_wrap(), creating separate distribution plots unique group facet variable. ncol single integer giving number columns facet layout. facet NULL, ncol must 1 number unique categories facet variable; values outside range result error. argument ignored facet NULL. group_counts logical flag. TRUE, sizes groups displayed inside rectangles plot created mosaic() function. FALSE (default), group sizes shown. group_counts_size single numeric value specifies size group count labels millimeters ('mm'). value passed size argument ggplot2::geom_text(). significance logical flag; defaults FALSE. TRUE, Chi-squared test independence performed contingency table y group. Note group must specified test calculated. facet provided, significance assessed separately facet subgroup. Additionally, function calculates standardized Pearson residuals (differences observed expected counts) fills mosaic plot cells based level partial significance cell. plot_name string specifying valid file name path plot. set NULL, plot displayed current graphical device saved locally. valid name .png .pdf extension provided, plot saved locally. Users can also include subdirectory plot_name. Ensure file path follows correct syntax operating system. overwrite logical flag (default FALSE) evaluated save.name argument provided. TRUE, function checks whether plot name already exists. , existing plot overwritten. FALSE plot name exists, error thrown. plot exists, plot saved normally. ... Additional arguments pass rstatix::chisq_test significance = TRUE.

title: Plot the Distribution of Categorical Covariates — mosaic
code: ## Example: Creating a Mosaic Plot of the Titanic Dataset ## This plot visualizes survival rates by gender across different passenger ## classes. By setting `significance = TRUE`, you can highlight statistically ## significant differences within each rectangle of the mosaic plot. library(ggplot2)  # Load Titanic dataset and convert to data frame titanic_df <- as.data.frame(Titanic)  # Expand the dataset by repeating rows according to 'Freq' titanic_long <- titanic_df[rep(   seq_len(nrow(titanic_df)),   titanic_df$Freq ), ]  # Remove the 'Freq' column as it is no longer needed titanic_long$Freq <- NULL  # Plot the data using mosaic() and modify the result using additional ggplot2 # functions p <- mosaic(   data = titanic_long,   y = Survived,   group = Sex,   facet = Class,   ncol = 2,   significance = TRUE,   plot_name = NULL )  p <- p +   theme_minimal()  p

what: Optimize the Matching Process via Random Search — optimize_gps
title: Optimize the Matching Process via Random Search — optimize_gps
text: optimize_gps() function performs random search identify optimal combinations parameters match_gps() estimate_gps() functions. goal maximize percentage matched samples (perc_matched) minimizing maximum standardized mean difference (smd), thereby improving overall balance covariates across treatment groups. function supports parallel execution foreach future packages, enabling multithreaded computation accelerate optimization process, particularly dealing large datasets complex parameter spaces.

title: Optimize the Matching Process via Random Search — optimize_gps
code: optimize_gps(   data = NULL,   formula,   ordinal_treat = NULL,   n_iter = 1000,   opt_args = NULL )

title: Optimize the Matching Process via Random Search — optimize_gps
text: data data.frame containing variables specified formula argument. opt_args used, data provided within opt_args must match input exactly. formula valid formula object used estimate generalized propensity scores (GPS). treatment variable appears left-hand side, covariates right-hand side. Interactions can specified using *. See stats::formula() estimate_gps() details. opt_args provided, formula within must identical argument. ordinal_treat atomic vector defining ordered levels treatment variable. confirms variable ordinal adjusts levels accordingly using factor(treat, levels = ordinal_treat, ordered = TRUE). passed directly estimate_gps(). NULL, ordinal GPS estimation methods polr excluded optimization. See estimate_gps() details. n_iter Integer. Number unique parameter combinations evaluate optimization. Higher values generally yield better results increase computation time. large datasets high-dimensional parameter spaces, increasing n_iter recommended. using parallel processing (n_cores > 1), performance gains become apparent larger n_iter. many cores iterations may introduce overhead reduce efficiency. opt_args object class "opt_args" containing optimization parameters argument settings. Use make_opt_args() create object. specifies search space GPS estimation matching procedure.

title: Optimize the Matching Process via Random Search — optimize_gps
text: S3 object class best_opt_result. core component data.frame containing parameter combinations results optimization procedure. can access using attr(result, "opt_results") calling View(result), result best_opt_result object. object contains following custom attributes: opt_results: data.frame optimization results. row corresponds unique parameter combination tested. complete description columns, see Details section. optimization_time: Time (seconds) taken optimization loop (.e., core -loop evaluates combinations). include time needed GPS estimation, pre-processing, merging results loop completion. large datasets, excluded steps can still substantial. combinations_tested: Total number unique parameter combinations evaluated optimization. smd_results: detailed table standardized mean differences (SMDs) pairwise treatment group comparisons covariates specified formula. used select_opt() function filter optimal models based covariate-level balance across groups. treat_names: character vector names unique treatment groups. model_covs: character vector listing model covariates (main effects interactions) used formula. names correspond variables shown smd_results table.

title: Optimize the Matching Process via Random Search — optimize_gps
text: output S3 object class best_opt_result. core component data.frame containing parameter settings best-performing models, grouped ranked based balance quality. Optimization results categorized seven bins based maximum standardized mean difference (SMD): 0.00-0.05 0.05-0.10 0.10-0.15 0.15-0.20 0.20-0.25 0.25-0.30 Greater 0.30 Within SMD group, parameter combination(s) achieving highest perc_matched (.e., percentage matched samples) selected. cases multiple combinations yield identical smd perc_matched, results retained. Combinations matching failed GPS estimation converge return NA result columns (e.g., perc_matched, smd). returned data.frame includes following columns (depending number treatment levels): iter_ID: Unique identifier parameter combination method_match: Matching method used match_gps(), e.g., "nnm" "fullopt" caliper: Caliper value used match_gps() order: Ordering GPS scores prior matching kmeans_cluster: Number k-means clusters used replace: Whether replacement used matching (nnm ) ties: Tie-breaking rule nearest-neighbor matching (nnm ) ratio: Control--treated ratio nnm min_controls, max_controls: Minimum maximum controls fullopt reference: Reference group used estimate_gps() match_gps() perc_matched: Percentage matched samples (balqual()) smd: Maximum standardized mean difference (balqual()) p_{group_name}: Percent matched per treatment group (based group s ample size) method_gps: GPS estimation method used (estimate_gps()) link: Link function used GPS model smd_group: SMD range category row resulting best_opt_result object also includes custom summary() method summarizes: number optimal parameter sets per SMD group associated SMD match rates Total combinations tested Total runtime optimization loop

title: Examine the Imbalance of Continuous Covariates — raincloud
text: raincloud() function allows generate distribution plots continuous data easy uncomplicated way. function based ggplot2 package, must already preinstalled Raincloud plots consist three main elements: Distribution plots, specifically  violin plots mean values standard deviations respective groups, Jittered point plots depicting underlying distribution data rawest form, Boxplots, summarizing important statistics underlying distribution.

title: Examine the Imbalance of Continuous Covariates — raincloud
code: raincloud(   data = NULL,   y = NULL,   group = NULL,   facet = NULL,   ncol = 1,   significance = NULL,   sig_label_size = 2L,   sig_label_color = FALSE,   smd_type = "mean",   density_scale = "area",   limits = NULL,   jitter = 0.1,   alpha = 0.4,   plot_name = NULL,   overwrite = FALSE,   ... )

title: Examine the Imbalance of Continuous Covariates — raincloud
text: data non-empty data.frame containing least one numeric column, specified y argument. argument must provided default value. y single string unquoted symbol representing name numeric column data. vector matching workflow, typically numeric covariate requires balancing. group single string unquoted symbol representing name factor character column data. raincloud() plots, groups specified group argument distinguished separate fill color aesthetics. clarity, recommended plot fewer 10 groups, though formal limit. facet single string unquoted symbol representing name variable data facet . argument used call ggplot2::facet_wrap(), creating separate distribution plots unique group facet variable. ncol single integer giving number columns facet layout. facet NULL, ncol must 1 number unique categories facet variable; values outside range result error. argument ignored facet NULL. significance single string specifying method calculating p-values multiple comparisons groups defined group argument. Significant comparisons represented bars connecting compared groups left side boxplots. Note many significant tests, plot size may adjust accordingly. available methods refer Details section. significance argument NULL, standardized mean differences (SMDs) also calculated displayed right side jittered point plots. sig_label_size single integer 1 20 specifying size significance standardized mean difference (SMD) labels shown left right side plot. sig_label_color Logical flag. FALSE (default), significance SMD bars text displayed default color (black). TRUE, colors applied dynamically based value: nonsignificant tests SMD values 0.10 displayed green, significant tests SMD values 0.10 higher displayed red. smd_type single string indicating type effect size calculate display left side jittered point plots: mean - Cohen's d calculated, median - Wilcoxon effect size (r) calculated based Z statistic extracted Wilcoxon test. density_scale Character(1). Scaling method violin density. "area": violins total area (default). "count": violin areas proportional number observations. "width": violins maximum height (width placed horizontally), regardless sample size. limits numeric atomic vector length two, specifying y axis limits distribution plots. first element sets minimum value, second sets maximum. vector passed ggplot2::xlim() function adjust axis scale. jitter single numeric value 0 1 controls amount jitter applied points ggplot2::geom_jitter() plots. Higher values jitter argument produce jittered plot. recommended keep value low, higher jitter can make plot difficult interpret. alpha single numeric value 0 1 controls transparency density plots, boxplots, jittered point plots. Lower values result higher transparency. recommended keep value relatively high maintain interpretability plots using group argument, excessive transparency may cause overlap groups, making difficult distinguish visually. plot_name string specifying valid file name path plot. set NULL, plot displayed current graphical device saved locally. valid name .png .pdf extension provided, plot saved locally. Users can also include subdirectory plot_name. Ensure file path follows correct syntax operating system. overwrite logical flag (default FALSE) evaluated save.name argument provided. TRUE, function checks whether plot name already exists. , existing plot overwritten. FALSE plot name exists, error thrown. plot exists, plot saved normally. ... Additional arguments passed function calculating p-values significance argument specified. available functions associated different significance methods, please refer Details section consult documentation relevant functions rstatix package.

text: Available methods argument significance : "t_test" - Performs pairwise comparison using two-sample t-test, default Holm adjustment multiple comparisons. test assumes normally distributed data equal variances. adjustment can modified via p.adjust.method argument. test implemented via rstatix::pairwise_t_test() "dunn_test" - Executes Dunn's test pairwise comparisons following Kruskal-Wallis test. non-parametric alternative t-test assumptions normality homogeneity variances violated. Implemented via rstatix::dunn_test(). "tukeyHSD_test" - Uses Tukey's Honest Significant Difference (HSD) test pairwise comparisons group means. Suitable comparing pairs overall ANOVA significant. method assumes equal variance groups implemented via rstatix::tukey_hsd(). "games_howell_test" - post-hoc test used ANOVA, assume equal variances equal sample sizes. ’s particularly robust data violate homogeneity variance assumptions. Implemented via rstatix::games_howell_test(). "wilcoxon_test" - Performs Wilcoxon rank-sum test (also known Mann-Whitney U test) non-parametric pairwise comparisons. Useful data normally distributed. Implemented via rstatix::pairwise_wilcox_test().

code: ## Example: Creating a raincloud plot for the ToothGrowth dataset. ## This plot visualizes the distribution of the `len` variable by ## `dose` (using different colors) and facets by `supp`. Group ## differences by `dose` are calculated using a `t_test`, and standardized ## mean differences (SMDs) are displayed through jittered points. library(ggplot2) library(ggpubr)  p <- raincloud(ToothGrowth, len, dose, supp,   significance = "t_test",   jitter = 0.15,   alpha = 0.4 )  ## As `p` is a valid `ggplot` object, we can manipulate its ## characteristics using the `ggplot2` or `ggpubr` packages ## to create a publication-grade plot: p <- p +   theme_classic2() +   theme(     axis.line.y = element_blank(),     axis.ticks.y = element_blank()   ) +   guides(fill = guide_legend("Dose [mg]")) +   ylab("Length [cm]")  p   ## Example: demonstrate `limits` and `plot_name` (no file is saved ## because `plot_name = NULL`) p2 <- raincloud(   ToothGrowth, len, dose, supp,   significance = "t_test",   limits = c(0, 40),   plot_name = NULL )  p2 #> Warning: Removed 29 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range #> (`geom_flat_violin()`).

title: Select Optimal Parameter Combinations from Optimization Results — select_opt
text: select_opt() helper function filter prioritize results optimize_gps() based specific goals study. Depending research design, certain pairwise comparisons treatment groups may important others. example: may want prioritize matching specific groups (e.g. specific disease vs. controls), ignoring group comparisons SMD evaluation. may wish retain many samples possible critical group set groups, regardless matching rates groups. function enables targeted selection optimal parameter combinations : Evaluating SMDs specific pairwise treatment group comparisons, Selecting key covariates assess balance, Prioritizing matched sample size selected treatment groups. combining criteria, select_opt() allows tailor optimization output study's focus - whether emphasizes covariate balance targeted group comparisons maximizing sample retention specific subgroups.

title: Select Optimal Parameter Combinations from Optimization Results — select_opt
code: select_opt(   x,   smd_groups = NULL,   smd_variables = NULL,   smd_type = c("mean", "max"),   perc_matched = NULL )

title: Select Optimal Parameter Combinations from Optimization Results — select_opt
text: x object class best_opt_result, produced optimize_gps() function. smd_groups list pairwise comparisons (character vectors length 2) specifying treatment group comparisons prioritized SMD evaluation. element must valid pair treatment levels. NULL, pairwise comparisons used. Example: list(c("adenoma", "crc_malignant"), c("controls", "adenoma")) smd_variables character vector covariate names include SMD evaluation. Must match variables listed attr(x, "model_covs"). smd_type character string ("mean" "max"), defining aggregate SMDs across covariates comparisons. "max" selects combinations lowest maximum SMD; "mean" uses average SMD. perc_matched character vector treatment levels matching rate maximized. NULL, overall perc_matched used. specified, sum matching percentages listed groups used selection within SMD category.

title: Select Optimal Parameter Combinations from Optimization Results — select_opt
text: S3 object class select_result, containing filtered prioritized optimization results. object includes: data.frame selected parameter combinations performance metrics. Attribute param_df: data.frame full parameter specifications (iter_ID, GPS/matching parameters, etc.), useful manually refitting reproducing results. object also includes custom print() method summarizes: Number selected combinations per SMD bin Corresponding aggregated SMD (mean max) Overall group-specific percentage matched

title: Select Optimal Parameter Combinations from Optimization Results — select_opt
text: Optimization results grouped bins based maximum SMD observed parameter combination. bins follow structure optimize_gps(): 0.00-0.05 0.05-0.10 0.10-0.15 0.15-0.20 0.20-0.25 0.25-0.30 0.30-0.35 0.35-0.40 0.40-0.45 0.45-0.50 0.50 Within bin, models first filtered based aggregated SMD across specified smd_groups smd_variables, using method defined smd_type. , among remaining models, best-performing one(s) selected based percentage matched samples - either overall specified treatment groups (perc_matched).

title: vecmatch: Vector Matching for Generalized Propensity Scores — vecmatch-package
text: vecmatch package implements vector matching methods based generalized propensity scores (GPS) balancing multiple treatment groups, along diagnostic tools visualization functions.

title: vecmatch: Vector Matching for Generalized Propensity Scores — vecmatch-package
text: vecmatch currently stable stage. core matching diagnostic functionality implemented covered tests, package actively maintained. Minor API changes may still occur response user feedback methodological development, major breaking changes anticipated. Future work focus extending set matching algorithms, adding diagnostics, improving performance documentation.
